module.name: cntr_3ud
module.clocking_model: Single-clock, positive-edge-triggered, three-bit modulo-8 counter. State changes only on a Verilog positive-edge transition.

up_down.role: Logic 1 decrements; logic 0, X, or Z takes the procedural if else branch and increments.
up_down.sampling: Sampled on each Verilog positive-edge transition of clk.
up_down.timing_contract: The value at the active clock event controls the next count.

clk.role: Clock; active edge is positive, including Verilog 0-to-1/X/Z and X/Z-to-1 transitions.
clk.timing_contract: A Verilog positive-edge transition triggers the state update.

reset.role: Active-high synchronous reset sampled on the active clock edge; X/Z follows procedural Verilog if semantics.
reset.sampling: Synchronous to clk; sampled only on its Verilog positive-edge transition.
reset.timing_contract: Reset assertion and release affect state only when sampled at an active clock event.

bin_count.role: Three-bit modulo-8 count; wraps on increment/decrement overflow.
bin_count.timing_contract: Updated after a Verilog positive-edge transition of clk.

declared_unknowns: The RTL does not initialize bin_count; its power-up value is unknown until a positive clock edge evaluates reset as logic 1.
The Verilog testbench changes reset at 25 ns, coincident with a positive clock edge, so the value sampled at that edge is scheduling-dependent.
The original testbench also drives up_down on the same positive edge at which the DUT samples it; this SystemC stimulus avoids that race and does not claim to reproduce its random sequence.
